overview: White develops the queen's bishop to b2 against the e5 pawn before committing the knights, a Nimzowitsch-Larsen style flank move on an e-pawn game. After 2...Nc6 3.Bb2 d6 4.Nf3 Black has an easy game, and White aims for a Hypermodern set-up with Nc3 and a slow plan against e5.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the queen's bishop and press e5.
Play Nf3 and Bb5 or Nc3 and f4 depending on Black's set-up.

black_ideas.idea: Develop naturally with ...Nc6 and ...d5 for a good centre.
Attack the b2 bishop's diagonal with ...f6 or ...Bd6.

typical_structures.structure: Black e5/d5 centre against a b2 bishop and flexible White pawns.

character.notes: Quiet, undemanding development; White has no direct threats.

soundness.notes: Sound but not testing; Black can take space.

structure.notes: Fluid centre with flank play; not decided.

approach.notes: Rarely used by strong players; mostly a surprise choice.

character.reason: Unforced, flexible play with no known sharp lines.

structure.reason: Flank-style development with the centre left open to change.

level.reason: Little theory but few forcing plans.

plans.reason: The b2 bishop is the whole idea.
